page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Hardware caching includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX functionality.

The hardware configuration provides 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering a generous ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The instance includes 69 GB of local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance placing in the top quartile. Single-threaded compression tasks demonstrate standard throughput, achieving 26.1 GB/sec in gzip. Conversely, multi-threaded capacity remains structurally limited by the single-core constraint, resulting in lower-tier Geekbench multi-core scores and multi-threaded stress-ng outputs. Memory bandwidth tests measure 32.63 GB/sec read and 22.38 GB/sec write on large blocks, while static web serving registers at 2.52 GB/sec and Redis operations reach 2.01 million operations per second.

By constraining CPU allocations while maintaining a high memory capacity, the E4-2as_v4 provides notable cost efficiency for memory-heavy applications where software licensing is pegged to core counts. Appropriate workloads include in-memory key-value caching, data buffering, ETL staging steps, and low-concurrency database systems requiring high RAM allocations relative to compute throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core, combined with 32.0 GB of system RAM and a bundled 69 GB local SSD, without GPU acceleration. The hardware configuration emphasizes memory density over parallel throughput, offering 16.0 GB per core. Benchmark results reflect this design with strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng alongside moderate single-core Geekbench and compression metrics. However, multi-core throughput, uncached memory bandwidth, and transaction-heavy operations like Redis are constrained by the single-core topology. This instance provides qualitative cost advantages for workloads governed by per-core software licensing, making it appropriate for lightweight databases, in-memory caching tiers, and memory-intensive background processing.
